To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of molecular cytogenetic analysis in POCs from pregnancies achieved by ART and NC, and selective biopsy by hystero-embryoscopy is essential for determining the cause of pregnancy failure and for avoiding the risk of maternal contamination.
the use of donor eggs from younger women, sperm with a high concentration, and NC pregnancies are associated with lower rates of chromosomal abnormalities in POCs.
the use of hysteroembryo-scopy for selective fetal tissue biopsy is an effective method for determining the cause of pregnancy failure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of chromosomal abnormalities in miscarriages from NC or ART pregnancies.
improving the reproductive prognosis for infertile couples by providing them with a better understanding of their reproductive potential and the risk factors associated with pregnancy loss.
the importance of the molecular analysis of POCs and the need for a selective biopsy of the embryo in the first trimester of pregnancy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the incidence of abnormal pregnancies is 62.7 %, with a higher incidence in pregnancies assisted by ART and a lower incidence in pregnancies assisted using donor eggs from young women.
chromosomal abnormalities are the most common cause of pregnancy loss, and the incidence of chromosomal anomalies is higher in pregnancies achieved through ART than in those conceived by NC.
ART-assisted pregnancies with a patient’s own eggs have a higher incidence of abnormal gestations than NC or ART-assisted pregnancies using donor eggs from young women.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
POC analysis is a very useful tool to determine the cause for miscarriage in infertile couples and to improve pregnancy rates in future pregnancies.
the incidence of chromosomal anomalies is higher in POC after assisted reproduction than in NC pregnancies.
the use of hysteroembryo-scopy and molecular cytogenetic analysis of POCs can help to identify the causes of pregnancy loss in infertile couples.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rate of chromosomally abnormal miscarriages was higher in POCs after ART using the patients’ own oocytes than in POCs from NC pregnancies.
POC analysis by molecular cytogenetics can help identify the causes of pregnancy loss and improve reproductive outcomes.
hysteroembryo-scopic biopsy is an effective and safe method to obtain fetal tissue for genetic analysis.
